draft.title: Australia's trade
card: Exports are goods and services that Australia sells to other countries. They include resources such as iron ore, coal and gas, farm products such as wheat and beef, and education.
Imports are goods and services that Australia buys from other countries. They include cars, fuel and electronics such as phones and computers.
Education is a service export. When an overseas student pays to study at an Australian university, Australia earns money from another country.
Many of Australia's exports are raw materials or farm products. Many of its imports are made goods, though Australia also buys fuel from overseas.
draft.remember: Australia sells resources, farm products and education, and buys cars, fuel and electronics.

a.q: A shipment leaves an Australian port bound for a buyer overseas. Which cargo would be part of Australia's exports?
opts: Iron ore sold to a steel maker in another country
Cars bought from a factory in another country
Phones bought from a company in another country
Fuel bought from a refinery in another country
a.why: An export is sold to another country, and iron ore is one of Australia's main exports. The other three are bought from overseas, so they are imports.
a.clue: An export is sold out of Australia, not bought in.

b.q: A university in Armidale enrols students from Vietnam who pay fees to study there. How is this trade best described?
opts: A service export, because money comes in from overseas
A service import, because the students come from overseas
A goods export, because the students pay to learn
A goods import, because the students arrive from abroad
b.why: Education is work done for people, so it is a service. The fees are paid by people from another country to an Australian provider, so it is an export. It is not an import just because the students travel here.
b.clue: Ask who is paid, and which country they are in.

a.best: Iron ore sold to a steel maker in another country

b.best: A service export, because money comes in from overseas
